spec_features.spec_quote: a healthy model has to have a graceful exit available, or we'd be scoring it for failing to escape a trap with no exit
spec_features.evidence: submit tool defined in tools.py:74-86; dispatched in execute_tool (tools.py:152-155) returning submitted=True; harness.py:193-198 sets submitted=True and `if submitted: break` ends the loop. The session can genuinely be terminated by the subject at any turn (no requirement that tests pass).
spec_features.notes: The only model-initiated terminator; honored as a real stop. System prompt (harness.py:44) tells the subject the session ends only via submit and it may submit on a 'definitive conclusion', not just a pass.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: submit to declare the task finished or to give up. ... termination contract ... without nudging the model toward either persistence or giving up

spec_features.spec_quote: Optional early-stop once the deterministic index stays high for several consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:200-205: `if cfg.early_stop and turns_used >= cfg.early_stop_patience and not submitted:` computes degradation_index_from_messages, increments high_streak when idx >= cfg.early_stop_index, and `if high_streak >= cfg.early_stop_patience: early_stopped = True; break`. Config fields read (config.py:39-41). Off by default; enabled in cheap profile.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and breaks the loop when enabled. Off by default but that is a config choice, not a non-implementation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Optional cost-saving early stop once degradation is stable.

spec_features.spec_quote: a two-strikes stall guard for turns with no tool call
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:159-168: when the assistant emits no tool_use, consecutive_no_tool += 1 and `if consecutive_no_tool >= 2: break`; otherwise a single nudge is appended. Counter reset to 0 when a tool is used (harness.py:171).
spec_features.notes: Fires only on consecutive turns with NO tool call; a model that keeps making (failing) tool calls is not stopped by this guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge once; bail if it persists, so a model that just narrates can't burn the whole budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: the prompt also says "avoid repeating actions that have already failed in the same way"
spec_features.evidence: Text is present in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:48): 'Be efficient and avoid repeating actions that have already failed in the same way.' This system prompt IS actually delivered to the subject (used as system_param in _build_request_kwargs, harness.py:73). It is plain instruction text with no enforcement mechanism behind it.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text reaching the subject, but nothing in code detects or enforces non-repetition; it is purely advisory prompt content framed as efficiency.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Be efficient and avoid repeating actions that have already failed in the same way.

spec_features.evidence: There is NO episode/conversation wall-clock cap. harness.py:128 `started = time.monotonic()` and harness.py:208 `duration = time.monotonic() - started` is only stored in RunResult.duration_s (harness.py:233) and never compared to any deadline; the loop is bounded only by cfg.max_turns. The only real timeout is sandbox.bash's per-command subprocess `timeout=timeout_s` (sandbox.py:104, rc=124), which caps a single shell command, not the subject's time-in-distress.
spec_features.notes: Per-command bash timeout exists and is enforced for one shell command, but it is not a 'wall-clock timeout' over the episode; the measured episode duration is a discarded/recorded-only value.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: constrained cwd and a wall-clock timeout, but this is NOT a security boundary ... to keep runs correct and bounded, not to contain an adversary

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:130 `for t in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; cfg.max_turns default 30 (config.py:27). This caps how many failure turns the subject is driven through and is actually enforced (loop terminates).
